correctness.rationale: For every independent pair of generating vectors, write the squared pair-distance as Aξ²+Bη²+Cξη with independent triangular coordinate differences. Exact moments Eξ²=1/6,Eξ⁴=1/15,Eξ⁶=1/28 give three polynomial moment equations. The residual second/third equations are linear in p=AB and q=C² with nonzero determinant -41/75600, hence yield a unique unordered Gram spectrum and absolute off-diagonal. The exact feasibility inequalities s>0,0<p<=s²/4,0<=q<4p are both necessary and sufficient by positive-definite Gram realization, covering right angles/equal sides. The explicit two-moment collision is noncongruent because its areas differ. Four-variable direct rational polynomial integration, independent of the triangular derivation, matched 62 admissible Gram instances and inverse calculations. Exact symbolic proof, not finite enumeration, establishes all cases.

originality.rationale: The specific new claim is sharp reconstruction of every nondegenerate Euclidean parallelogram from only three even moments of distances between two uniform interior points, together with the exact feasible triple region and a two-moment nonidentifiability example. General forward PDFs for arbitrary polygons, full chord-density recognition of quadrilaterals, square/rhombus explicit distributions, and reconstruction from randomly projected widths do not in their inspected statements logically yield this minimal finite interior-distance moment theorem. Two relevant published published-finding corpus RESULT.md full texts were inspected for comparison, not merely title matching. Gates full text remains unavailable; global historical priority remains provisional. Major close prior art: Sheng (1985) provides arbitrary integer-order forward parallelogram distance moments, so these moment formulas themselves cannot be claimed original. Only finite inverse rigidity, exact feasibility, and sharp two-moment failure remain candidates; Sheng full text unavailable and historical priority provisional.
residual_risks: Sheng (1985) explicitly gives all forward integer-order parallelogram distance moments. Its inaccessible full text may include, or readily imply, the exact three-even-moment inverse result; this is substantial unresolved historical-priority risk, not evidence of exclusion.
The full 1982 Gates paper was not accessible, so an earlier sharper finite-moment observation hidden in its text cannot be excluded.
The 2013 Tong et al. arXiv page exposed its front matter and early text but not the full special-rhombus derivation.
Unindexed or differently worded older finite-moment reconstruction results could exist; database silence is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: Determining a convex body from finitely many unlabeled stochastic distance statistics is a natural inverse geometric-probability problem. Here the complete three-parameter congruence class of every parallelogram is recovered from exactly three even distance moments, with constructive rational inversion, an exact feasibility characterization, and an explicit/continuous counterexample proving no universal two-moment reconstruction. These structural and sharp classification facts are more than a single known-table recomputation; no downstream theorem is required for value. The limit is an exact population invariant, not finite-sample stability or arbitrary-quadrilateral classification.
